# Validator fixtures

Test data for `tests/test_validate.py`. Two vaults, whose content is fictional and carries no evidential weight.

- `minimal/` — one complete valid pass from source to chapter: one source per source type (document, publication, data), one distillate each, one assertion grounded across all three, one output paragraph with a grounded footnote and a posit. Its `knowledge/state.md` carries the source inventory `tools/inventory.py` generates from that file state. `python tools/validate.py tests/fixtures/minimal` passes clean and without a warning, computations included.
- `broken/` — the specimens of the defects the validator must catch, errors and warnings alike. Which specimen carries which finding is registered in `tests/test_validate.py`, where `BROKEN_FINDINGS` pins each sub-rule of an error code to its specimen and a part of its message, and the warning tests name their specimens one by one. Its `knowledge/state.md` carries the source inventory `tools/inventory.py` generates from that file state, including the rows of specimens that break the schema. Each fixture names its own defect in its lead sentence.

The suite runs the validator over both and asserts that `minimal/` produces nothing and that every registered finding in `broken/` is caught, which is what establishes that the validator catches anything at all. Both state documents are held against the generator output, so an inventory that falls behind its fixture fails the suite. A further test parses the finding codes out of `tools/validate.py` and holds them against the specimen registries in `tests/test_validate.py`, so a check that gains no specimen and a specimen whose check disappeared both fail the suite. Deleting the fixtures leaves those tests running against directories that do not exist, where passing means nothing.

The validator reads only the content folders at the root it is given, so the fixtures stay invisible to a run over the vault itself and can be broken deliberately without touching the evidence layer.
